name: Psychology
notice: Education, not diagnosis or therapy. PsychGradify teaches psychology. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and haven't yet been reviewed by subject experts, so they may contain errors; check important points against your course materials. Its demonstrations of personality, cognition and mood are learning tools, not validated tests, and nothing here can diagnose a condition, offer treatment or replace a qualified professional. If you are worried about your mental health, speak to your GP or NHS 111; in an emergency call 999 or Samaritans on 116 123 (UK).

paths.name: A level Psychology
paths.sub: The core of A level and equivalent courses: approaches, biopsychology, memory, attachment, social influence, psychopathology and research methods.

paths.name: University year 1
paths.sub: The first-year core of a psychology degree: foundations, biological, cognitive, developmental and social psychology, with methods and statistics.

paths.name: Research skills
paths.sub: From a research question to a reported result: design, ethics, measurement, statistics and open science.

paths.name: Mind and brain
paths.sub: Neurones, brain systems, perception, memory, learning and the new computational theories of mind.

paths.name: Mental health
paths.sub: How mental disorders are understood, classified and treated, in context and across cultures. Educational, not clinical advice.

paths.name: Applied psychology
paths.sub: Psychology at school, at work, in health, sport, law and the design of technology.

paths.name: People and society
paths.sub: Development, social behaviour, personality, culture and evolution: psychology's bridge to SocGradify.

lessons.title: The peripheral nervous system: somatic and autonomic
The cerebral cortex and the four lobes
The limbic system: hippocampus and amygdala
Brain imaging: EEG, MRI, fMRI and PET
Long-term memory: episodic, semantic and procedural
The fundamental attribution error and self-serving bias
Measures of dispersion: range, variance and standard deviation
Type I and Type II errors
Theories of emotion: James–Lange and Cannon–Bard
Open science and the replication crisis

interactives.title: Brain anatomy explorer
interactives.sub: Side and midline views of the brain: select any region to see what it does and the classic evidence for it.
interactives.note: Schematic and not to scale; functions depend on networks, not single regions.

interactives.title: Find the brain region
interactives.sub: You're given a region: find it on the side or midline view. Build a streak.
interactives.note: Schematic and not to scale.

interactives.title: Neurone and action potential
interactives.sub: The Hodgkin–Huxley model: find the threshold, the refractory period and repetitive firing; block channels with toxins.
interactives.note: SciGradify Biology's simulation: the published 1952 equations for one patch of squid axon membrane, with no propagation or myelin.

interactives.title: Synaptic transmission
interactives.sub: Calcium entry, vesicle release, receptors and breakdown at a cholinergic synapse, with drugs and toxins: summation, agonists and antagonists.
interactives.note: SciGradify Biology's simulation: a small kinetic model with illustrative values; the sequence of events is accurate.

interactives.title: Neurotransmitter and receptor explorer
interactives.sub: Glutamate, GABA, dopamine, serotonin, noradrenaline, acetylcholine and endorphins: receptors, roles and the drugs that act on them. Then sort agonists from antagonists.
interactives.note: Mechanisms simplified for study; most drugs act on more than one system.

interactives.title: Lateralisation and the split brain
interactives.sub: Predict what split-brain patients say and do when information reaches only one hemisphere.
interactives.note: Based on Sperry's and Gazzaniga's published findings; scenarios simplified.

interactives.title: Sleep and circadian rhythms
interactives.sub: The two-process model: sleep pressure and the circadian clock across three days. Stay up late, cut sleep short or shift your schedule.
interactives.note: Time constants from Daan, Beersma and Borbély (1984); circadian curve idealised; the clock doesn't re-entrain.

interactives.title: The physiology of stress
interactives.sub: Step through the fast SAM pathway and the slower HPA axis, cortisol's negative feedback and what changes under chronic stress.
interactives.note: An illustrative sequence of established physiology; real responses overlap and vary.

interactives.title: The Stroop task
interactives.sub: Name ink colours while ignoring the words, or the side a word appears on, and measure your own interference effect.
interactives.note: Your own response times, measured in the browser; a classroom demonstration, not a research-grade measure.

interactives.title: Visual search: features and conjunctions
interactives.sub: Find the orange X among distractors. Does it pop out, or do you have to search item by item?
interactives.note: Your own response times; a replication of Treisman and Gelade's (1980) paradigm with simplified displays.

interactives.title: Free recall and the serial position curve
interactives.sub: Learn a 15-word list and recall it, straight away or after a distractor task, and plot primacy and recency.
interactives.note: Your own recall, scored by exact spelling; one person's curve is noisy until you have several runs.

interactives.title: Digit span
interactives.sub: Measure your short-term memory span, then try chunking.
interactives.note: A standard forward digit span procedure with two attempts per length.

interactives.title: Models of memory
interactives.sub: The multi-store model and the working memory model, component by component, with the evidence for and against each.
interactives.note: Summaries of the published models.

interactives.title: Choice reaction time (Hick's law)
interactives.sub: Respond to one, two or four possible lights and see whether your reaction time rises with the information in the choice.
interactives.note: Your own response times measured in the browser.

interactives.title: The Müller-Lyer illusion
interactives.sub: Adjust a line to match one with fins, measure your illusion, and weigh the competing explanations.
interactives.note: Your own judgements; explanations of the illusion are contested.

interactives.title: Signal detection
interactives.sub: Separate sensitivity (d′) from response bias: move the criterion, watch hits and false alarms trade off, and trace the ROC curve.
interactives.note: The equal-variance Gaussian model; values are exact.

interactives.title: Cognitive and attribution bias explorer
interactives.sub: Answer the classic framing, conjunction, anchoring, base-rate and availability problems, and attribution scenarios, then compare yourself with the original participants.
interactives.note: Published results quoted from the original papers; problems paraphrased.

interactives.title: Classical conditioning
interactives.sub: The Rescorla–Wagner model: acquisition, extinction and blocking, and what changes with salience and the size of the reward.
interactives.note: The published 1972 model; it cannot produce spontaneous recovery, which the notes discuss.

interactives.title: Schedules of reinforcement
interactives.sub: Cumulative records for continuous, fixed and variable ratio and interval schedules, and what happens in extinction.
interactives.note: Response rules chosen to reproduce the patterns Ferster and Skinner (1957) described; not data from an animal.

interactives.title: Behavioural data: an ABAB design
interactives.sub: Read a single-case reversal graph by level, trend and variability, and see how effect size and noise change what you can conclude.
interactives.note: Simulated observations of an invented pupil.

interactives.title: Developmental timeline
interactives.sub: Piaget's stages, Erikson's psychosocial stages, attachment phases and language milestones on one lifespan.
interactives.note: Typical ages from the theories' authors; stage theories are contested.

interactives.title: Strange Situation scenarios
interactives.sub: Classify invented infants' attachment from their reunion behaviour, then evaluate the method across cultures.
interactives.note: Invented scenarios for applying Ainsworth's and Main and Solomon's categories.

interactives.title: Line judgements: a conformity procedure
interactives.sub: Judge 18 sets of lines after six simulated group members answer, then compare your result with Asch's.
interactives.note: Simulated group members, and you know it, so this demonstrates the procedure rather than the pressure of a real group.

interactives.title: The Big Five, explained
interactives.sub: Describe a fictional character on the five factors and read what each trait means and what research links it to.
interactives.note: An educational demonstration, not a personality test.

interactives.title: Interpreting psychometric scores
interactives.sub: Convert between z, T and standard scores and percentiles, and see how reliability sets the confidence band around a score.
interactives.note: Exact normal-distribution values; the scores are invented for practice, not from a real test.

interactives.title: A CBT thought record
interactives.sub: Help an invented client complete a thought record, from the situation to a balanced thought.
interactives.note: Educational simulation of a standard CBT technique; not therapy.

interactives.title: Case formulation: the 5 Ps
interactives.sub: Sort an invented client's difficulties into presenting, predisposing, precipitating, perpetuating and protective factors.
interactives.note: An invented vignette for learning the structure of a formulation.

interactives.title: Experiment builder
interactives.sub: Make the design decisions for nine studies: variables, hypotheses, designs, confounds, sampling, controls, analysis and ethics.
interactives.note: Invented studies; standard design decisions.

interactives.title: Study critique
interactives.sub: Find the key flaw in six invented studies: causation, power, demand, p-hacking, WEIRD samples and attrition.
interactives.note: Invented study summaries.

interactives.title: Sampling simulator
interactives.sub: Draw hundreds of samples by random, stratified, opportunity and volunteer methods and compare their bias and standard error.
interactives.note: SocGradify's simulation: a simulated population of 10,000 with invented response patterns.

interactives.title: Statistics workspace: describing data
interactives.sub: Paste in data or generate a set: mean, median, mode, SD, skew, kurtosis, standard error, a confidence interval and a histogram.
interactives.note: Sample statistics (n − 1); example data simulated.

interactives.title: Correlation and regression visualiser
interactives.sub: Anscombe's quartet and your own points: Pearson's r, Spearman's ρ, the regression line, R² and residuals.
interactives.note: Anscombe's (1973) data are real; your own points are illustrative.

interactives.title: Crosstabs and chi-square
interactives.sub: Row percentages, expected counts, χ² and Cramér's V for a two-by-two table.
interactives.note: Example counts invented; enter counts from a real table.

interactives.title: Hypothesis-test simulator
interactives.sub: Run one study or a thousand: p-values, power, Type I and II errors and the winner's curse, with an independent t-test.
interactives.note: Simulated samples from normal populations with a true effect you choose.
